analysis.overall: You spent 84% of the day in range with a solid average of 135 mg/dL, though post-meal timing led to significant spikes after lunch and dinner, as well as a sharp morning roller coaster.

events.title: Post-lunch peak
events.description: After a 50g carb lunch at 12:49 PM, glucose steadily climbed over two hours to a peak of 220 mg/dL before multiple correction boluses brought it back to baseline.

events.title: Dinner spike
events.description: A 40g carb dinner at 8:02 PM pushed glucose up to 214 mg/dL before stacked micro-corrections helped ease it back into range overnight.

events.title: Early morning low
events.description: Glucose drifted low in the quiet early morning hours down to 63 mg/dL, but smoothly rebounded into safe territory within an hour.

events.title: Breakfast dip and rebound spike
events.description: Insulin for a 70g breakfast acted faster than carb absorption, triggering a low of 61 mg/dL before the delayed carbs pushed glucose up past 200 mg/dL.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Carb absorption lagged behind insulin at breakfast, causing a low followed by a spike—consider pre-bolus timing or meal composition for larger carb loads.
